title: MEDI2004 W6 · Ion Channels & Channelopathies
subject: Pharmacology Fundamentals
content: Channels = gated proteins (open/closed/inactivated), not holes. Cav: 4 domains x 6 TM (S1-S6); S4 = voltage sensor; P-loop (S5-S6) = selectivity filter. Filters: GYG (K+), EEEE (Ca2+), DEKA (Na+); selectivity is chemical (dehydration energetics), not size -> larger K+ passes, smaller Na+ rejected. TTX/saxitoxin plug Na+ filter. Electrochemical gradient = electrical + diffusion; Nernst EK ~ -90 mV, ENa ~ +60 mV, resting -70 mV. Na/K-ATPase: 3 Na out / 2 K in per ATP (active); channels passive/fast/no ATP. AP: rest -70 -> Na+ in via Nav to +30 (depolarise) -> Nav inactivate + Kv open, K+ out (repolarise) -> undershoot; Nav has activation (S4) + inactivation (ball-and-chain) gates -> refractory. Saltatory conduction jumps nodes of Ranvier. Local anaesthetics (lidocaine) bind inactivated Nav state (state/use-dependent block). Architectures: nAChR 5-fold non-selective cation (ligand-gated; vecuronium competitive, succinylcholine depolarising); ClC 2-fold Cl- dimer; Kv/Nav/Cav 4-fold. Ca channels: brain LTP + NT release (N/PQ), heart pacemaking (L-type), pancreas insulin (ATP closes K-ATP -> depolarise -> Cav -> Ca -> exocytosis; sulfonylureas block K-ATP), muscle E-C coupling (DHP + ryanodine; malignant hyperthermia = ryanodine GoF). CFTR (dF508 misfold) -> cystic fibrosis. Channelopathy rule 1: same gene GoF/LoF -> opposite diseases (Nav1.5 LQT3 GoF vs Brugada LoF). Rule 2: different genes -> same disease (LQT from Nav1.5 GoF or hERG LoF). Nav1.1 (SCN1A) LoF spectrum -> febrile seizures to Dravet. hERG promiscuous cavity -> drug-induced LQT (safety screen). T-type Cav3.x low threshold ~-70 mV, burst firing, DRG, injury upregulation; ethosuximide blocks Cav3.1 for absence epilepsy. Gating states + window current; state-dependent (use-dependent) block. Na blockers: lidocaine, phenytoin, carbamazepine. Cav blockers: DHPs (amlodipine, vascular, outer site) vs PAAs (verapamil, cardiac, pore plug). Ziconotide (cone snail, N-type, intrathecal pain). Same drug = medicine or poison depending on dose/route/cell type.
